turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Sorry we're late, doctor. The Luas sat at Charlemont for ages and then the car park was full, I was pure mortified coming in the door.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): You're grand. Sit down.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Desperate rain as well. Left the umbrella on the bus, typical.
[SEG0004] person_4 (NURSE): Notes are here. I did her blood pressure outside.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm.
[SEG0006] person_1 (PATIENT): Umm I had a whole list in my notebook and then I forgot the notebook on the kitchen table, which is just like me, but anyway that's not why we're here.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Why are you here?

[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): Err I'm pregnant, about sixteen weeks, and I'm worried the baby could have thalasemia. Himself was told at a blood camp that he carries the trait, and I've been sick with the worry.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): When was the camp?
[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): Uh I cannot pin the date. It was last summer, or maybe after the October bank holiday, I go over it and I still haven't a clue.
[SEG0011] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The letter said beta thalassaemia trait. It came to the house after the GAA club session.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any bleeding?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): No bleeding. Not a spot, I've been checking every day since the positive test, probably more than any sensible person would, sorry.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Pain?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): No pain. There is a heavy tiredness though, and uh I couldn't tell you when that began, last winter or the one before, it all runs together.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sleeping?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): Sleep's been rotten. I lie there going through the what-ifs since the letter came.
[SEG0018] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She's awake half the night. I'm anxious too, but sure I'm not the patient.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Medicines?

[SEG0020] person_1 (PATIENT): I take folick acid by mouth every morning for the pregnancy. I told the midwife five milligrams, that was wrong, it's the 400 microgram bit inside the pregnicare tablet from the chemist.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Allergies?
[SEG0022] person_1 (PATIENT): No. No drug allergies and no food allergies.
[SEG0023] person_4 (NURSE): My own sister was told she was a carrier and her little lad is in senior infants now and flying it. I only say that so people don't panic in the corridor.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): I never smoked. I used to have a glass of wine on a Friday and that's stopped since the test turned positive, not a drop.

[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): The trait means one haemoglobin gene is altered. The red cells come out smaller. It doesn't make him ill by itself. If both of ye carry it there's a one in four chance of the full condition in the child.

[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): So he's not sick? I read three websites, they contradicted each other, and my cousin went on about a neighbour's child who needs transfusions, and I spiralled, which I do.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. He's not sick from the trait. Working impression is a possible risk to the baby only if you carry it too. Not confirmed.
[SEG0029] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): They mentioned my haemoglobin was low, something like 12, but that was my old result.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): We won't use his figure. Nurse, today's numbers?
[SEG0031] person_4 (NURSE): Blood pressure 118 over 74, pulse 86, oxygen 98 percent.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Abdomen is soft. No pallor. The womb feels about right for sixteen weeks.
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): I say sixteen weeks because it's tidy, but the twelve-week scan was fifteen plus a few days and I always round it up, my mother says I over-explain everything.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Your mother's health?
[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): Mam has high blood pressure. Nothing like thalassaemia on my side, that anyone ever said.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll book a full blood count and a haemoglobin electrophoresis for you today. That's the screen.
[SEG0037] person_1 (PATIENT): Today, even though I had toast and tea? I always get in a knot about fasting rules and then I end up describing my breakfast, which nobody needs.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): No fasting needed. If the bloods show you carry it as well, we might refer ye to genetic counselling. I'm not booking that now.
[SEG0039] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And if she's clear?
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Then this doesn't put the baby at risk of the major illness. I'll see ye back in two weeks with the results.
[SEG0041] person_1 (PATIENT): Do I stay on the pregnicare?
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, stay on it. If you get bleeding or bad pain, come straight in, don't wait.
[SEG0043] person_1 (PATIENT): I will. The notebook had about twenty questions, half of them daft, but the baby was the only one that mattered.
[SEG0044] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We'll come back. Thanks, doctor.
[SEG0045] person_4 (NURSE): Reception will send ye to phlebotomy on the way out. I'm off at four, so it won't be me.
[SEG0046] person_1 (PATIENT): Thanks a million. Sorry again for landing in late.

spec.situation: Couple, wife pregnant, husband found to carry thalassaemia trait at a camp; both anxious; blood tests for the wife planned; genetic counselling discussed.

traps.happens: The conversation OPENS with a remark, joke, apology for being late, small talk, or a trigger event (a relative's diagnosis, a neighbour's advice, the receptionist's note) BEFORE the real reason is stated. The patient states the real concern a few turns later.
traps.label_rule: chief_complaint is the real concern in a short phrase in the patient's wording (e.g. 'worried about diabetes', 'voice gets tired'). NOT the opening remark, the joke or the trigger (the relative's illness goes into family_history only if it is a relative's condition said as such).

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

features: vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.

bad.reason: Beta thalassaemia trait reported by family member is supported; relation 'husband' not explicitly stated.
Worry/anxiousness is present, but certainty 'certain' overstates; patient sounds worried rather than explicitly diagnosing anxiety.
Pregnancy supported, but duration 'approximately 15 weeks and several days' is not stated as actual duration; patient says about sixteen weeks and rounds up.
bad.text: pregnancy (status=existing, duration=approximately 15 weeks and several days, reported_by=patient)

bad.reason: Explanation given, but status 'recommended' is wrong; this was performed counselling, not a recommendation.
bad.text: Explained that thalassaemia trait is one altered haemoglobin gene, smaller red cells, not an illness alone, and a one in four chance of major thalassaemia if both parents are carriers (action_type=counselling, status=recommended, responsible_person=doctor)

omissions.text: Allergy history was specified as no drug allergies and no food allergies, not just generic 'allergies absent'.
Doctor advised that no fasting was needed for the planned blood tests.
Doctor said he was not booking genetic counselling at this time, only considering it if her bloods show she is also a carrier.
Doctor stated that if she is clear/not a carrier, this does not put the baby at risk of the major illness.
